answer:
Multi-Sensor Motion Record Audit — completed. All six required artifacts were produced by a single executed end-to-end script (analysis.py) and are keyed below by their exact native relative output paths.

**Fitted parameters (strictly on the 700 'train' rows; SEs from profile-likelihood curvature / Procrustes information):**
- gyro_bias_rad_s = **−0.0252916 ± 0.0020** rad/s
- time_offset_s = **−0.0075281 ± 0.0087** s (convention: lidar interval [t0, t1] corresponds to IMU-clock interval [t0+τ, t1+τ])
- yaw_extrinsic_rad = **−0.0336377 ± 0.0050** rad

**ψ convention statement (recorded verbatim in metrics.json):** sensor-to-body convention — a vector expressed in the lidar frame maps to the body frame via v_b = Rz(ψ)·v_l, equivalently angle(Δp_l) = Δθ/2 − ψ. task_info.json contains no wording disambiguating the generator's convention (verified by full-file keyword scan), so the standard sensor-to-body convention was adopted and explicitly recorded; the opposite convention would flip the sign and is unresolvable from the data.

**Held-out validation (154 rows, used only for residuals.csv and diagnostics, never for fitting):** yaw residual RMS = 0.005901 rad (train 0.005820, both ≈ declared σ_yaw = 0.006; white, per-segment offset F-test p = 0.34, homogeneous noise model retained); translation (chord) residual RMS = 0.017871 m (train 0.017405, ≈ declared σ_trans = 0.018). An independent brute-force recomputation of all 154 held-out yaw residuals from the raw gyro samples matches residuals.csv to 5e-11 rad.

**residual_trans_m definition (documented in metrics.json and as a comment in analysis.py):** ‖Rz(ψ)·dp_l − L̂·[cos(Δθ/2), sin(Δθ/2)]‖₂ in metres — the 2-D mismatch between the measured lidar relative translation rotated into the body frame with the calibrated extrinsic and the chord predicted from the calibrated gyro heading change (unicycle arc); effectively the calibrated cross-track/chord-geometry mismatch, since a single-axis gyro cannot constrain the along-track component.

**Observability ranking rationale (larger score = more useful for constraining the reported quantities):** per-segment Fisher-style information computed from train rows only — per-scan sensitivity of the yaw residual to τ (Σ(ω(t1+τ)−ω(t0+τ))²/σ_yaw²), bias lever (ΣΔt²/σ_yaw²), and translation lever for ψ (Σ L²/σ_trans²) — each component normalized by its maximum over segments and combined with the task's own parameter weights (τ 0.4, b 0.25, ψ 0.35). Ranking: segment 3 (0.873) > 1 (0.818) > 8 (0.612) > 4 (0.610) > 0 (0.575) > 5 (0.548) > 7 (0.547) > 2 (0.444) > 6 (0.421): windows with strong rotation-rate change across scan edges (3, 1) constrain the time offset and extrinsic best; nearly-straight windows (2, 6) constrain least.

Diagnostics in calibration_diagnostics.png (six panels: gyro stream with segment shading, heading consistency, yaw residuals vs time for train+heldout with ±2σ bands, residual histogram vs Gaussian, translation residuals vs Δθ, profile-cost-vs-τ identifiability curve); metrics.json additionally carries parameters with SEs and tolerance bands, conventions, per-channel residual RMS/mean, per-segment score components, and the structure audit. Known limitation carried from the approved plan: τ is weakly identifiable (SE 0.0087 s vs full band 0.0015 s, zero band 0.015 s), and the ψ sign convention is the one assumption data cannot resolve; both are honestly recorded in metrics.json.

payload.psi_convention: sensor-to-body: v_b = Rz(psi)*v_l, angle(dp_l) = dtheta/2 - psi; recorded in metrics.json
payload.residual_trans_m_definition: || Rz(psi)*dp_l - Lhat*[cos(dtheta/2), sin(dtheta/2)] ||_2 (calibrated cross-track/chord-geometry mismatch, metres)
